body_markdown: Microsoft’s move towards hybrid intelligence on Windows is an important development for how organisations should think about AI architecture. With user permission, Copilot will increasingly use local PC context, take actions on the device, and tap into local models when that makes sense, while still reaching the cloud when more capability is required. Microsoft describes this as intelligent routing between local and cloud AI rather than assuming every task should go straight to the cloud. For businesses, this changes the architecture discussion from: device → cloud AI → answer to: device → intelligent routing → local model or cloud model → action That creates some clear opportunities around latency, cloud consumption and keeping certain processing closer to the device, but it also adds another design decision: where should inference actually happen? For future AI solutions, local versus cloud processing should become part of the architecture conversation alongside security, permissions, governance, cost and user experience. And “local” should never automatically be interpreted as “safe”. Local agents and models still need controls around files, credentials, outputs, retention and the actions they are allowed to take.
